founderDecisionRecommendations.F4-divine-ruach: Accept the genre-based split: lower-case 'spirit' in Isaiah's endowment/outpouring poetry and 'ruach' in Kings/Ezekiel agent narratives. The weak point is Ezekiel's own endowment/outpouring verses: 37:14 'I will put my ruach in you' is published, and 36:27 and 39:29 are not yet translated in this data. These share Isaiah's sense rather than the 'agent that lifts' sense that justifies transliteration. At the next Ezekiel pass, decide whether those few sites should move to 'my spirit' or stay 'ruach' for in-book consistency. Either way, add reciprocal cross-references 44:3 ↔ Ezek 37:14 now, and to 39:29 once it is translated. Do not transliterate in Isaiah.

paragraphs.text: וְעַתָּ֥ה שְׁמַ֖ע יַעֲקֹ֣ב עַבְדִּ֑י וְיִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל בָּחַ֥רְתִּי בֽוֹ׃

i18n.en: But now hear, O Jacob my servant, and Israel whom I have chosen:
i18n.he: וְעַתָּ֥ה שְׁמַ֖ע יַעֲקֹ֣ב עַבְדִּ֑י וְיִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל בָּחַ֥רְתִּי בֽוֹ׃

paragraphs.text: כֹּה־אָמַ֨ר יְהוָ֥ה עֹשֶׂ֛ךָ וְיֹצֶרְךָ֥ מִבֶּ֖טֶן יַעְזְרֶ֑ךָּ אַל־תִּירָא֙ עַבְדִּ֣י יַֽעֲקֹ֔ב וִישֻׁר֖וּן בָּחַ֥רְתִּי בֽוֹ׃

i18n.en: Thus says YHWH, who made you and formed you from the womb, who will help you: Do not fear, O Jacob my servant, and Jeshurun whom I have chosen.
i18n.he: כֹּה־אָמַ֨ר יְהוָ֥ה עֹשֶׂ֛ךָ וְיֹצֶרְךָ֥ מִבֶּ֖טֶן יַעְזְרֶ֑ךָּ אַל־תִּירָא֙ עַבְדִּ֣י יַֽעֲקֹ֔ב וִישֻׁר֖וּן בָּחַ֥רְתִּי בֽוֹ׃

notes.official: *ʿōśeḵā wᵉyōṣerḵā mib-beṭen* “who made you and formed you from the womb” (central `asah`, `yatsar`). *yᵉšurûn* “Jeshurun” is a poetic name for Israel (Deut 32:15; 33:5, 26), probably from *yāšār* “upright.” *ʿaḇdî* is rendered plainly (overlay `eved-servant-identity-isaiah`).

paragraphs.text: כִּ֤י אֶצָּק־מַ֙יִם֙ עַל־צָמֵ֔א וְנֹזְלִ֖ים עַל־יַבָּשָׁ֑ה אֶצֹּ֤ק רוּחִי֙ עַל־זַרְעֶ֔ךָ וּבִרְכָתִ֖י עַל־צֶאֱצָאֶֽיךָ׃

i18n.en: For I will pour water on the thirsty, and streams on the dry ground; I will pour my spirit upon your seed, and my blessing upon your offspring;
i18n.he: כִּ֤י אֶצָּק־מַ֙יִם֙ עַל־צָמֵ֔א וְנֹזְלִ֖ים עַל־יַבָּשָׁ֑ה אֶצֹּ֤ק רוּחִי֙ עַל־זַרְעֶ֔ךָ וּבִרְכָתִ֖י עַל־צֶאֱצָאֶֽיךָ׃

notes.official: *ʾeṣṣōq rûḥî ʿal-zarʿeḵā* “I will pour my spirit upon your seed,” in parallel with “my blessing upon your offspring” and with the water poured on the thirsty land. *rûaḥ* is lower-case “spirit,” as in NRSV and NJPS (ASV “my Spirit”; overlay `ruach-divine-spirit-lower-case-isaiah`). Ezekiel uses the same image (Ezek 39:29), where the corpus transliterates “ruach”; the cross-book difference is flagged in the wave report.

paragraphs.text: וְצָמְח֖וּ בְּבֵ֣ין חָצִ֑יר כַּעֲרָבִ֖ים עַל־יִבְלֵי־מָֽיִם׃

i18n.en: and they shall spring up among the grass, like willows by flowing streams.
i18n.he: וְצָמְח֖וּ בְּבֵ֣ין חָצִ֑יר כַּעֲרָבִ֖ים עַל־יִבְלֵי־מָֽיִם׃

paragraphs.text: זֶ֤ה יֹאמַר֙ לַֽיהוָ֣ה אָ֔נִי וְזֶ֖ה יִקְרָ֣א בְשֵֽׁם־יַעֲקֹ֑ב וְזֶ֗ה יִכְתֹּ֤ב יָדוֹ֙ לַֽיהוָ֔ה וּבְשֵׁ֥ם יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל יְכַנֶּֽה׃ (פ)

i18n.en: This one will say, “I am YHWH's,” and another will call himself by the name of Jacob; and another will write on his hand, “YHWH's,” and take the name of Israel as a title.
i18n.he: זֶ֤ה יֹאמַר֙ לַֽיהוָ֣ה אָ֔נִי וְזֶ֖ה יִקְרָ֣א בְשֵֽׁם־יַעֲקֹ֑ב וְזֶ֗ה יִכְתֹּ֤ב יָדוֹ֙ לַֽיהוָ֔ה וּבְשֵׁ֥ם יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל יְכַנֶּֽה׃ (פ)

notes.official: *wᵉzeh yiḵtōḇ yāḏô la-YHWH* “and another will write on his hand, ‘YHWH’s.’” The words can mean a mark of ownership written or tattooed on the hand (NRSV, NJPS; cf. Ezek 9:4) or a signature to a deed, “subscribe with his hand unto YHWH” (ASV). The line follows the modern versions. *yᵉḵanneh* is “take as a title, surname himself.”

paragraphs.text: כֹּֽה־אָמַ֨ר יְהוָ֧ה מֶֽלֶךְ־יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל וְגֹאֲל֖וֹ יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֑וֹת אֲנִ֤י רִאשׁוֹן֙ וַאֲנִ֣י אַחֲר֔וֹן וּמִבַּלְעָדַ֖י אֵ֥ין אֱלֹהִֽים׃

i18n.en: Thus says YHWH, the King of Israel, and his Redeemer, YHWH of hosts: I am the first and I am the last, and besides me there is no God.
i18n.he: כֹּֽה־אָמַ֨ר יְהוָ֧ה מֶֽלֶךְ־יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל וְגֹאֲל֖וֹ יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֑וֹת אֲנִ֤י רִאשׁוֹן֙ וַאֲנִ֣י אַחֲר֔וֹן וּמִבַּלְעָדַ֖י אֵ֥ין אֱלֹהִֽים׃

notes.official: *ʾănî rîšôn wa-ʾănî ʾaḥărôn ûmib-balʿāḏay ʾên ʾĕlōhîm* “I am the first and I am the last, and besides me there is no God.” Absolute *ʾĕlōhîm* in the denial formula is “God” (ASV), the book’s practice for every form of the word. NRSV and NJPS print lower-case “god” to show that the class itself is denied; the capital follows the ASV base and the overlay’s earlier “God” renderings (overlay `elohim-el-eloah-monotheistic-formula-isaiah`). The central “the Elohim” convention, scoped to the Genesis narrative, is not extended. The verse is among the clearest statements of monotheism in the Hebrew Bible, and the line leaves its grammar as it is.

paragraphs.text: וּמִֽי־כָמ֣וֹנִי יִקְרָ֗א וְיַגִּידֶ֤הָ וְיַעְרְכֶ֙הָ֙ לִ֔י מִשּׂוּמִ֖י עַם־עוֹלָ֑ם וְאֹתִיּ֛וֹת וַאֲשֶׁ֥ר תָּבֹ֖אנָה יַגִּ֥ידוּ לָֽמוֹ׃

i18n.en: And who is like me? Let him proclaim it, let him declare it and set it in order for me, since I appointed the ancient people; and the things that are coming and what will come, let them declare.
i18n.he: וּמִֽי־כָמ֣וֹנִי יִקְרָ֗א וְיַגִּידֶ֤הָ וְיַעְרְכֶ֙הָ֙ לִ֔י מִשּׂוּמִ֖י עַם־עוֹלָ֑ם וְאֹתִיּ֛וֹת וַאֲשֶׁ֥ר תָּבֹ֖אנָה יַגִּ֥ידוּ לָֽמוֹ׃

paragraphs.text: אַֽל־תִּפְחֲדוּ֙ וְאַל־תִּרְה֔וּ הֲלֹ֥א מֵאָ֛ז הִשְׁמַעְתִּ֥יךָ וְהִגַּ֖דְתִּי וְאַתֶּ֣ם עֵדָ֑י הֲיֵ֤שׁ אֱל֙וֹהַּ֙ מִבַּלְעָדַ֔י וְאֵ֥ין צ֖וּר בַּל־יָדָֽעְתִּי׃

i18n.en: Do not dread, and do not be afraid; have I not told you from of old and declared it? And you are my witnesses. Is there a God besides me? There is no rock; I know of none.
i18n.he: אַֽל־תִּפְחֲדוּ֙ וְאַל־תִּרְה֔וּ הֲלֹ֥א מֵאָ֛ז הִשְׁמַעְתִּ֥יךָ וְהִגַּ֖דְתִּי וְאַתֶּ֣ם עֵדָ֑י הֲיֵ֤שׁ אֱל֙וֹהַּ֙ מִבַּלְעָדַ֔י וְאֵ֥ין צ֖וּר בַּל־יָדָֽעְתִּי׃

notes.official: *hă-yēš ʾĕlôah mib-balʿāḏay* “Is there a God besides me?” *ʾĕlôah*, the singular of *ʾĕlōhîm*, is used here as a synonym of the *ʾĕlōhîm* of v. 6. The Translator applied the central `shaddai-eloah` entry (“Eloah,” scoped to Job). The Editor declines it, because transliterating one of the three synonyms in a single formula (*ʾĕlōhîm* 44:6, *ʾĕlôah* 44:8, *ʾēl* 45:21) would mark a distinction the text does not make. ASV has “a God” (overlay `elohim-el-eloah-monotheistic-formula-isaiah`). *wᵉʾên ṣûr* “there is no rock”: *ṣûr* is lower-case as a divine epithet, as at 26:4 (overlay `yah-tzur-olamim-everlasting-rock-isaiah-26`; ASV “Rock”).

paragraphs.text: יֹֽצְרֵי־פֶ֤סֶל כֻּלָּם֙ תֹּ֔הוּ וַחֲמוּדֵיהֶ֖ם בַּל־יוֹעִ֑ילוּ וְעֵדֵיהֶ֣ם הֵׄ֗מָּׄהׄ בַּל־יִרְא֛וּ וּבַל־יֵדְע֖וּ לְמַ֥עַן יֵבֹֽשׁוּ׃

i18n.en: Those who form carved images are all of them emptiness, and the things they delight in do not profit; their own witnesses neither see nor know, that they may be put to shame.
i18n.he: יֹֽצְרֵי־פֶ֤סֶל כֻּלָּם֙ תֹּ֔הוּ וַחֲמוּדֵיהֶ֖ם בַּל־יוֹעִ֑ילוּ וְעֵדֵיהֶ֣ם הֵׄ֗מָּׄהׄ בַּל־יִרְא֛וּ וּבַל־יֵדְע֖וּ לְמַ֥עַן יֵבֹֽשׁוּ׃

notes.official: *yōṣᵉrê-p̄esel kullām tōhû* “those who form carved images are all of them emptiness” (overlay `tohu-bare-emptiness-wasteland-isaiah`). In *wᵉʿēḏêhem hēmmāh* “their own witnesses, they …,” the pronoun הֵמָּה bears the *puncta extraordinaria*, dots over each letter, one of the places where the Masoretes marked a word as doubtful. The dots are kept in the source text, and the word is translated (overlay `mt-qere-textual-policy-isaiah`). The satire on idol-making (vv. 9–20) is prose-like and is often attributed to a later hand. It is translated as it stands.

paragraphs.text: מִֽי־יָצַ֥ר אֵ֖ל וּפֶ֣סֶל נָסָ֑ךְ לְבִלְתִּ֖י הוֹעִֽיל׃

i18n.en: Who has formed a god, or cast a carved image that profits nothing?
i18n.he: מִֽי־יָצַ֥ר אֵ֖ל וּפֶ֣סֶל נָסָ֑ךְ לְבִלְתִּ֖י הוֹעִֽיל׃

paragraphs.text: הֵ֤ן כָּל־חֲבֵרָיו֙ יֵבֹ֔שׁוּ וְחָרָשִׁ֥ים הֵ֖מָּה מֵֽאָדָ֑ם יִֽתְקַבְּצ֤וּ כֻלָּם֙ יַֽעֲמֹ֔דוּ יִפְחֲד֖וּ יֵבֹ֥שׁוּ יָֽחַד׃

i18n.en: Behold, all his companions shall be put to shame, and the craftsmen are only human; let them all gather together, let them stand up; they shall be in dread, they shall be put to shame together.
i18n.he: הֵ֤ן כָּל־חֲבֵרָיו֙ יֵבֹ֔שׁוּ וְחָרָשִׁ֥ים הֵ֖מָּה מֵֽאָדָ֑ם יִֽתְקַבְּצ֤וּ כֻלָּם֙ יַֽעֲמֹ֔דוּ יִפְחֲד֖וּ יֵבֹ֥שׁוּ יָֽחַד׃

paragraphs.text: חָרַ֤שׁ בַּרְזֶל֙ מַֽעֲצָ֔ד וּפָעַל֙ בַּפֶּחָ֔ם וּבַמַּקָּב֖וֹת יִצְּרֵ֑הוּ וַיִּפְעָלֵ֙הוּ֙ בִּזְר֣וֹעַ כֹּח֔וֹ גַּם־רָעֵב֙ וְאֵ֣ין כֹּ֔חַ לֹא־שָׁ֥תָה מַ֖יִם וַיִּיעָֽף׃

i18n.en: The ironsmith takes a cutting tool and works it over the coals; he forms it with hammers and works it with his strong arm; he grows hungry and his strength fails; he drinks no water and is faint.
i18n.he: חָרַ֤שׁ בַּרְזֶל֙ מַֽעֲצָ֔ד וּפָעַל֙ בַּפֶּחָ֔ם וּבַמַּקָּב֖וֹת יִצְּרֵ֑הוּ וַיִּפְעָלֵ֙הוּ֙ בִּזְר֣וֹעַ כֹּח֔וֹ גַּם־רָעֵב֙ וְאֵ֣ין כֹּ֔חַ לֹא־שָׁ֥תָה מַ֖יִם וַיִּיעָֽף׃

paragraphs.text: חָרַ֣שׁ עֵצִים֮ נָ֣טָה קָו֒ יְתָאֲרֵ֣הוּ בַשֶּׂ֔רֶד יַעֲשֵׂ֙הוּ֙ בַּמַּקְצֻע֔וֹת וּבַמְּחוּגָ֖ה יְתָאֳרֵ֑הוּ וַֽיַּעֲשֵׂ֙הוּ֙ כְּתַבְנִ֣ית אִ֔ישׁ כְּתִפְאֶ֥רֶת אָדָ֖ם לָשֶׁ֥בֶת בָּֽיִת׃

i18n.en: The carpenter stretches out a line; he marks it out with a stylus; he works it with planes and marks it out with the compass; he makes it in the figure of a man, with the beauty of a human being, to dwell in a house.
i18n.he: חָרַ֣שׁ עֵצִים֮ נָ֣טָה קָו֒ יְתָאֲרֵ֣הוּ בַשֶּׂ֔רֶד יַעֲשֵׂ֙הוּ֙ בַּמַּקְצֻע֔וֹת וּבַמְּחוּגָ֖ה יְתָאֳרֵ֑הוּ וַֽיַּעֲשֵׂ֙הוּ֙ כְּתַבְנִ֣ית אִ֔ישׁ כְּתִפְאֶ֥רֶת אָדָ֖ם לָשֶׁ֥בֶת בָּֽיִת׃

notes.official: The carpenter’s tools: *qāw* “line,” *śereḏ* “stylus” (or red chalk, a hapax), *maqṣuʿôṯ* “planes” (or chisels), *mᵉḥûgāh* “compass.” *kᵉṯip̄ʾereṯ ʾāḏām lāšeḇeṯ bāyiṯ* “with the beauty of a human being, to dwell in a house,” that is, to stand in a shrine.

paragraphs.text: לִכְרָת־ל֣וֹ אֲרָזִ֔ים וַיִּקַּ֤ח תִּרְזָה֙ וְאַלּ֔וֹן וַיְאַמֶּץ־ל֖וֹ בַּעֲצֵי־יָ֑עַר נָטַ֥ע אֹ֖רֶן וְגֶ֥שֶׁם יְגַדֵּֽל׃

i18n.en: He cuts down cedars for himself, and takes a holm tree and an oak, and lets it grow strong for himself among the trees of the forest; he plants a fir, and the rain makes it grow.
i18n.he: לִכְרָת־ל֣וֹ אֲרָזִ֔ים וַיִּקַּ֤ח תִּרְזָה֙ וְאַלּ֔וֹן וַיְאַמֶּץ־ל֖וֹ בַּעֲצֵי־יָ֑עַר נָטַ֥ע אֹ֖רֶן וְגֶ֥שֶׁם יְגַדֵּֽל׃

paragraphs.text: וְהָיָ֤ה לְאָדָם֙ לְבָעֵ֔ר וַיִּקַּ֤ח מֵהֶם֙ וַיָּ֔חָם אַף־יַשִּׂ֖יק וְאָ֣פָה לָ֑חֶם אַף־יִפְעַל־אֵל֙ וַיִּשְׁתָּ֔חוּ עָשָׂ֥הוּ פֶ֖סֶל וַיִּסְגָּד־לָֽמוֹ׃

i18n.en: Then it becomes fuel for a man; he takes some of it and warms himself; he kindles a fire and bakes bread; also he makes a god and worships it; he makes it a carved image and bows down to it.
i18n.he: וְהָיָ֤ה לְאָדָם֙ לְבָעֵ֔ר וַיִּקַּ֤ח מֵהֶם֙ וַיָּ֔חָם אַף־יַשִּׂ֖יק וְאָ֣פָה לָ֑חֶם אַף־יִפְעַל־אֵל֙ וַיִּשְׁתָּ֔חוּ עָשָׂ֥הוּ פֶ֖סֶל וַיִּסְגָּד־לָֽמוֹ׃

notes.official: *ʾap̄-yip̄ʿal-ʾēl wayyištāḥû* “also he makes a god and worships it.” *ʾēl* here is the idol and is lower-case “a god” (overlay `elohim-el-eloah-monotheistic-formula-isaiah`). *wayyisgāḏ* “and bows down” is the Aramaic-type verb *sāgaḏ* (Dan 3), used only in this passage in the Hebrew Bible (vv. 15, 17, 19; 46:6).

paragraphs.text: חֶצְיוֹ֙ שָׂרַ֣ף בְּמוֹ־אֵ֔שׁ עַל־חֶצְיוֹ֙ בָּשָׂ֣ר יֹאכֵ֔ל יִצְלֶ֥ה צָלִ֖י וְיִשְׂבָּ֑ע אַף־יָחֹם֙ וְיֹאמַ֣ר הֶאָ֔ח חַמּוֹתִ֖י רָאִ֥יתִי אֽוּר׃

i18n.en: Half of it he burns in the fire; over the half he eats meat; he roasts a roast and is satisfied; he also warms himself and says, “Aha, I am warm, I have seen the fire!”
i18n.he: חֶצְיוֹ֙ שָׂרַ֣ף בְּמוֹ־אֵ֔שׁ עַל־חֶצְיוֹ֙ בָּשָׂ֣ר יֹאכֵ֔ל יִצְלֶ֥ה צָלִ֖י וְיִשְׂבָּ֑ע אַף־יָחֹם֙ וְיֹאמַ֣ר הֶאָ֔ח חַמּוֹתִ֖י רָאִ֥יתִי אֽוּר׃

paragraphs.text: וּשְׁאֵ֣רִית֔וֹ לְאֵ֥ל עָשָׂ֖ה לְפִסְל֑וֹ יסגוד־[יִסְגָּד־] ל֤וֹ וְיִשְׁתַּ֙חוּ֙ וְיִתְפַּלֵּ֣ל אֵלָ֔יו וְיֹאמַר֙ הַצִּילֵ֔נִי כִּ֥י אֵלִ֖י אָֽתָּה׃

i18n.en: And the rest of it he makes into a god, his carved image; he bows down to it and worships, and prays to it and says, “Deliver me, for you are my god!”
i18n.he: וּשְׁאֵ֣רִית֔וֹ לְאֵ֥ל עָשָׂ֖ה לְפִסְל֑וֹ יסגוד־[יִסְגָּד־] ל֤וֹ וְיִשְׁתַּ֙חוּ֙ וְיִתְפַּלֵּ֣ל אֵלָ֔יו וְיֹאמַר֙ הַצִּילֵ֔נִי כִּ֥י אֵלִ֖י אָֽתָּה׃

notes.official: Ketiv/Qere. The consonantal יסגוד *yisgôḏ* is read יִסְגָּד *yisgāḏ* “he bows down,” a difference of vowel only (overlay `mt-qere-textual-policy-isaiah`). *lᵉʾēl … ʾēlî ʾāttāh* “into a god … you are my god”: lower-case for the idol.

paragraphs.text: לֹ֥א יָדְע֖וּ וְלֹ֣א יָבִ֑ינוּ כִּ֣י טַ֤ח מֵֽרְאוֹת֙ עֵֽינֵיהֶ֔ם מֵהַשְׂכִּ֖יל לִבֹּתָֽם׃

i18n.en: They do not know, nor do they understand; for their eyes are plastered over so that they cannot see, and their hearts so that they cannot understand.
i18n.he: לֹ֥א יָדְע֖וּ וְלֹ֣א יָבִ֑ינוּ כִּ֣י טַ֤ח מֵֽרְאוֹת֙ עֵֽינֵיהֶ֔ם מֵהַשְׂכִּ֖יל לִבֹּתָֽם׃

paragraphs.text: וְלֹא־יָשִׁ֣יב אֶל־לִבּ֗וֹ וְלֹ֨א דַ֥עַת וְלֹֽא־תְבוּנָה֮ לֵאמֹר֒ חֶצְי֞וֹ שָׂרַ֣פְתִּי בְמוֹ־אֵ֗שׁ וְ֠אַף אָפִ֤יתִי עַל־גֶּחָלָיו֙ לֶ֔חֶם אֶצְלֶ֥ה בָשָׂ֖ר וְאֹכֵ֑ל וְיִתְרוֹ֙ לְתוֹעֵבָ֣ה אֶעֱשֶׂ֔ה לְב֥וּל עֵ֖ץ אֶסְגּֽוֹד׃

i18n.en: And no one considers in his heart, nor is there knowledge or understanding to say, “Half of it I burned in the fire; I also baked bread on its coals; I roast meat and eat it; and shall I make the rest of it an abomination? Shall I bow down to a block of wood?”
i18n.he: וְלֹא־יָשִׁ֣יב אֶל־לִבּ֗וֹ וְלֹ֨א דַ֥עַת וְלֹֽא־תְבוּנָה֮ לֵאמֹר֒ חֶצְי֞וֹ שָׂרַ֣פְתִּי בְמוֹ־אֵ֗שׁ וְ֠אַף אָפִ֤יתִי עַל־גֶּחָלָיו֙ לֶ֔חֶם אֶצְלֶ֥ה בָשָׂ֖ר וְאֹכֵ֑ל וְיִתְרוֹ֙ לְתוֹעֵבָ֣ה אֶעֱשֶׂ֔ה לְב֥וּל עֵ֖ץ אֶסְגּֽוֹד׃

notes.official:
*wᵉyiṯrô lᵉṯôʿēḇāh ʾeʿĕśeh lᵉḇûl ʿēṣ ʾesgôḏ* has no interrogative particle. ASV, NRSV and NJPS read two indignant questions, “shall I make the rest of it an abomination? Shall I bow down to a block of wood?” This continues the man’s reasoning, which the verse says he never gets as far as. The line keeps the questions. *bûl ʿēṣ* is “a block of wood” (ASV “the stock of a tree”).

**Wheel of Heaven reading (reception note, not a translation claim).** *The Book Which Tells the Truth* (ch. 5) quotes v. 19 as statements (« et je tirerai du reste une abomination ! J’adorerai un bout de bois ! ») and applies the “piece of wood” to the cross. The Hebrew satirizes the carved idol of vv. 9–17, and the line follows the standard question reading.

paragraphs.text: רֹעֶ֣ה אֵ֔פֶר לֵ֥ב הוּתַ֖ל הִטָּ֑הוּ וְלֹֽא־יַצִּ֤יל אֶת־נַפְשׁוֹ֙ וְלֹ֣א יֹאמַ֔ר הֲל֥וֹא שֶׁ֖קֶר בִּימִינִֽי׃ (ס)

i18n.en: He feeds on ashes; a deluded heart has led him astray, and he cannot deliver his soul, nor say, “Is there not a lie in my right hand?”
i18n.he: רֹעֶ֣ה אֵ֔פֶר לֵ֥ב הוּתַ֖ל הִטָּ֑הוּ וְלֹֽא־יַצִּ֤יל אֶת־נַפְשׁוֹ֙ וְלֹ֣א יֹאמַ֔ר הֲל֥וֹא שֶׁ֖קֶר בִּימִינִֽי׃ (ס)

paragraphs.text: זְכָר־אֵ֣לֶּה יַעֲקֹ֔ב וְיִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל כִּ֣י עַבְדִּי־אָ֑תָּה יְצַרְתִּ֤יךָ עֶֽבֶד־לִי֙ אַ֔תָּה יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל לֹ֥א תִנָּשֵֽׁנִי׃

i18n.en: Remember these things, O Jacob, and Israel, for you are my servant; I formed you; you are my servant; O Israel, you will not be forgotten by me.
i18n.he: זְכָר־אֵ֣לֶּה יַעֲקֹ֔ב וְיִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל כִּ֣י עַבְדִּי־אָ֑תָּה יְצַרְתִּ֤יךָ עֶֽבֶד־לִי֙ אַ֔תָּה יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל לֹ֥א תִנָּשֵֽׁנִי׃

paragraphs.text: מָחִ֤יתִי כָעָב֙ פְּשָׁעֶ֔יךָ וְכֶעָנָ֖ן חַטֹּאותֶ֑יךָ שׁוּבָ֥ה אֵלַ֖י כִּ֥י גְאַלְתִּֽיךָ׃

i18n.en: I have blotted out your transgressions like a thick cloud, and your sins like a mist; return to me, for I have redeemed you.
i18n.he: מָחִ֤יתִי כָעָב֙ פְּשָׁעֶ֔יךָ וְכֶעָנָ֖ן חַטֹּאותֶ֑יךָ שׁוּבָ֥ה אֵלַ֖י כִּ֥י גְאַלְתִּֽיךָ׃

paragraphs.text: רָנּ֨וּ שָׁמַ֜יִם כִּֽי־עָשָׂ֣ה יְהוָ֗ה הָרִ֙יעוּ֙ תַּחְתִּיּ֣וֹת אָ֔רֶץ פִּצְח֤וּ הָרִים֙ רִנָּ֔ה יַ֖עַר וְכָל־עֵ֣ץ בּ֑וֹ כִּֽי־גָאַ֤ל יְהוָה֙ יַֽעֲקֹ֔ב וּבְיִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל יִתְפָּאָֽר׃ (פ)

i18n.en: Sing for joy, O skies, for YHWH has done it; shout, O depths of the earth; break forth into singing, O mountains, O forest and every tree in it! For YHWH has redeemed Jacob, and will glorify himself in Israel.
i18n.he: רָנּ֨וּ שָׁמַ֜יִם כִּֽי־עָשָׂ֣ה יְהוָ֗ה הָרִ֙יעוּ֙ תַּחְתִּיּ֣וֹת אָ֔רֶץ פִּצְח֤וּ הָרִים֙ רִנָּ֔ה יַ֖עַר וְכָל־עֵ֣ץ בּ֑וֹ כִּֽי־גָאַ֤ל יְהוָה֙ יַֽעֲקֹ֔ב וּבְיִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל יִתְפָּאָֽר׃ (פ)

notes.official: *rānnû šāmayim … hārîʿû taḥtîyôṯ ʾāreṣ* “Sing for joy, O skies … shout, O depths of the earth.” The height and depth of creation are summoned as a merism, in the physical register (“skies”) of the central *šāmayim* rule. *kî-ʿāśāh YHWH* “for YHWH has done it.”

paragraphs.text: כֹּֽה־אָמַ֤ר יְהוָה֙ גֹּאֲלֶ֔ךָ וְיֹצֶרְךָ֖ מִבָּ֑טֶן אָנֹכִ֤י יְהוָה֙ עֹ֣שֶׂה כֹּ֔ל נֹטֶ֤ה שָׁמַ֙יִם֙ לְבַדִּ֔י רֹקַ֥ע הָאָ֖רֶץ מי אתי [מֵאִתִּֽי׃]

i18n.en: Thus says YHWH, your Redeemer, who formed you from the womb: I am YHWH, who makes all things, who alone stretched out the skies, who spread out the earth by myself;
i18n.he: כֹּֽה־אָמַ֤ר יְהוָה֙ גֹּאֲלֶ֔ךָ וְיֹצֶרְךָ֖ מִבָּ֑טֶן אָנֹכִ֤י יְהוָה֙ עֹ֣שֶׂה כֹּ֔ל נֹטֶ֤ה שָׁמַ֙יִם֙ לְבַדִּ֔י רֹקַ֥ע הָאָ֖רֶץ מי אתי [מֵאִתִּֽי׃]

notes.official: Ketiv/Qere. The verse ends with consonants that can be read two ways. The ketiv מי אתי *mî ʾittî* asks “who was with me?” (ASV “who is with me?”, printed as a parenthesis), and the qere מֵאִתִּי *mēʾittî* says “by myself.” Both deny that anyone helped. The qere is read: “who spread out the earth by myself” (overlay `mt-qere-textual-policy-isaiah`). *ʿōśeh kōl* “who makes all things” (central `asah`); *nōṭeh šāmayim lᵉḇaddî* “who alone stretched out the skies” (creation register, see 40:12).

paragraphs.text: מֵפֵר֙ אֹת֣וֹת בַּדִּ֔ים וְקֹסְמִ֖ים יְהוֹלֵ֑ל מֵשִׁ֧יב חֲכָמִ֛ים אָח֖וֹר וְדַעְתָּ֥ם יְשַׂכֵּֽל׃

i18n.en: who frustrates the signs of the babblers, and makes fools of diviners; who turns the wise back, and makes their knowledge foolish;
i18n.he: מֵפֵר֙ אֹת֣וֹת בַּדִּ֔ים וְקֹסְמִ֖ים יְהוֹלֵ֑ל מֵשִׁ֧יב חֲכָמִ֛ים אָח֖וֹר וְדַעְתָּ֥ם יְשַׂכֵּֽל׃

paragraphs.text: מֵקִים֙ דְּבַ֣ר עַבְדּ֔וֹ וַעֲצַ֥ת מַלְאָכָ֖יו יַשְׁלִ֑ים הָאֹמֵ֨ר לִירוּשָׁלִַ֜ם תּוּשָׁ֗ב וּלְעָרֵ֤י יְהוּדָה֙ תִּבָּנֶ֔ינָה וְחָרְבוֹתֶ֖יהָ אֲקוֹמֵֽם׃

i18n.en: who confirms the word of his servant, and fulfills the counsel of his messengers; who says of Jerusalem, “She shall be inhabited,” and of the cities of Judah, “They shall be built, and I will raise up their ruins”;
i18n.he: מֵקִים֙ דְּבַ֣ר עַבְדּ֔וֹ וַעֲצַ֥ת מַלְאָכָ֖יו יַשְׁלִ֑ים הָאֹמֵ֨ר לִירוּשָׁלִַ֜ם תּוּשָׁ֗ב וּלְעָרֵ֤י יְהוּדָה֙ תִּבָּנֶ֔ינָה וְחָרְבוֹתֶ֖יהָ אֲקוֹמֵֽם׃

paragraphs.text: הָאֹמֵ֥ר לַצּוּלָ֖ה חֳרָ֑בִי וְנַהֲרֹתַ֖יִךְ אוֹבִֽישׁ׃

i18n.en: who says to the deep, “Be dry, and I will dry up your rivers”;
i18n.he: הָאֹמֵ֥ר לַצּוּלָ֖ה חֳרָ֑בִי וְנַהֲרֹתַ֖יִךְ אוֹבִֽישׁ׃

paragraphs.text: הָאֹמֵ֤ר לְכ֙וֹרֶשׁ֙ רֹעִ֔י וְכָל־חֶפְצִ֖י יַשְׁלִ֑ם וְלֵאמֹ֤ר לִירוּשָׁלִַ֙ם֙ תִּבָּנֶ֔ה וְהֵיכָ֖ל תִּוָּסֵֽד׃ (ס)

i18n.en: who says of Cyrus, “He is my shepherd, and he shall fulfill all my purpose,” saying of Jerusalem, “She shall be built,” and of the temple, “Your foundation shall be laid.”
i18n.he: הָאֹמֵ֤ר לְכ֙וֹרֶשׁ֙ רֹעִ֔י וְכָל־חֶפְצִ֖י יַשְׁלִ֑ם וְלֵאמֹ֤ר לִירוּשָׁלִַ֙ם֙ תִּבָּנֶ֔ה וְהֵיכָ֖ל תִּוָּסֵֽד׃ (ס)

notes.official: *hā-ʾōmēr lᵉḵôreš rōʿî* “who says of Cyrus, ‘He is my shepherd.’” Cyrus II of Persia, who took Babylon in 539 BCE, is named here and at 45:1. *hêḵāl* is “the temple” (overlay `heikhal-temple-palace-isaiah`).
